title: MoE-Infinity: Efficient MoE Inference on Personal Machines with Sparsity-Aware Expert Cache (Xue, Fu, Lu, Mai, Marina; arXiv 2401.14361, v1 25 Jan 2024, v3 12 Mar 2025)
setting: DeepSeek and Mixtral families; GPU-limited personal machines; batch 1; hardware not named on the abstract page; baselines vLLM, Ollama, DeepSpeed, BrainStorm
headline: 3.1-16.7x per-token latency improvement (abstract); tables not read
transfers_to_us: no: GPU cache with GPU-offload baselines; none of them is an SSD path with LRU
caveat: Baselines are GPU-oriented offloaders, so the multiplier says nothing about a CPU path that already has a cache. Only the abstract page was read (no tables).
notes: Reuse of a small expert set within one request at batch 1 is the paper's stated motive, which supports per-sequence caching as a concept but it is request-trace-driven, not ARC.

title: DAOP: Data-Aware Offloading and Predictive Pre-Calculation for Efficient MoE Inference (Zhang, Aggarwal, Mitra; DATE 2025; arXiv 2501.10375)
setting: Mixtral 8x7B and Phi-3.5-MoE; i9-10980XE CPU 130 GB + RTX A6000 48 GB, PCIe 4; batch 1; baselines MoE-OnDemand, DeepSpeed-MII, Mixtral-Offloading, Fiddler
headline: up to 8.20x over caching/prefetch, 1.35x over offloading (abstract); 4.52 tok/s Mixtral and 8.21 Phi-3.5 vs Fiddler +40.4% at 256/512 tokens; avg +35.4% across cache sizes
transfers_to_us: no: GPU+CPU compute split, cache ratio relative to GPU slots, HF Transformers
caveat: Placement is decided during prefill and fixed during decode; it is not a continuously adapting per-sequence cache, and it does not stream from disk.
notes: The catalog line (per-sequence allocation already published) is true but omits that placement is frozen after prefill.

title: OD-MoE: On-Demand Expert Loading for Cacheless Edge-Distributed MoE Inference (Wang, Du, Pan, Liew, Liu, Chen; CUHK; arXiv 2512.03927v1, 3 Dec 2025)
setting: Mixtral-8x7B; 10 nodes (main 1x RTX3090, shadow 2x RTX3090, 8 workers 1x RTX3090 each, 128-192 GB DRAM), 1 Gbps Ethernet; baselines HF Transformers, llama.cpp CPU, Mixtral-Offloading, MoE-Infinity, HOBBIT, AdapMoE
headline: 3.69 tok/s decode = 75.5% of Transformers (4.89), 4.49x llama.cpp (0.82); expert prediction recall 99.94/97.34/95.67% (FP16/INT8/NF4 shadow); TTFT about 2244 ms vs 417 ms
transfers_to_us: no: GPU nodes, expert loading into worker GPUs from their RAM, cacheless by design, 8 experts only
caveat: Hardware is ten GPU hosts; a quantized shadow model predicts experts several layers ahead, which is the real contribution.
notes: Last 14 characters of the page text not read (no effect on results).

title: Understanding MoE Offloading (SomeOddCodeGuy, DEV Community, 13 Oct 2025) [catalog calls it llama.cpp RPC backend / mac-tensor]
setting: gpt-oss-120b (about 120B total, 5.1B active, 36 layers, 128 experts, top-4) with llama.cpp --n-cpu-moe on a 24 GB GPU
headline: no throughput results; arithmetic of dense (about 1.5B) vs expert (about 3.5B) active parameters
transfers_to_us: no: CPU-GPU split over PCIe, not experts over a network
caveat: The page says nothing about the llama.cpp RPC backend, mac-tensor or network experts.
notes: Url does not support the catalog summary. A real source for llama.cpp RPC (docs or repo) is needed.

title: 1.5 TB of VRAM on Mac Studio - RDMA over Thunderbolt 5 (Jeff Geerling, 18 Dec 2025) [url slug says 15-tb]
setting: 4x M3 Ultra Mac Studio (2x512 GB + 2x256 GB), TB5 full mesh, RDMA; exo; also llama.cpp RPC
headline: Page text: Qwen3 235B about 32 tok/s and Kimi K2 Thinking about 30 tok/s on the full cluster; DeepSeek V3.1 numbers are only in a chart (21.1/27.8/32.5 not confirmable); TB5 50-60 Gbps real; RDMA latency about 300 us to under 50 us (cited MLX PR)
transfers_to_us: no: weights stay resident in each node's RAM (model split across nodes); no thin client fetches weights per token
caveat: The catalog's DeepSeek numbers cannot be confirmed from page text, and Kimi is about 30, not 28. Cluster cost about 40,000 USD.
notes: Notes llama.cpp RPC scales but is inefficient (more nodes means slower).

title: OD-MoE (the catalog url points to the wrong paper: it is FIRM-MoE, Chen et al., AAAI-26 vol 40 no 24, pp 20190-20198, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v40i24.39106)
setting: FIRM-MoE: expert offloading with fine-grained sub-experts, multi-layer prediction, resource-adaptive preload; hardware not given on the page
headline: FIRM-MoE: up to 1.5x decoding speedup and 2.8x memory saving vs offloading baselines (abstract). OD-MoE itself is the arXiv paper in P-0213 (ten nodes, 1 GbE, 3.69 tok/s)
transfers_to_us: OD-MoE (via P-0213): no. FIRM-MoE: unclear (hardware unknown)
caveat: Url is wrong for the stated paper; the row duplicates P-0213.
notes: Transport not confirmed on the AAAI page; the arXiv OD-MoE page gives 1 Gbps Ethernet.

title: Broadcast Rate Limits in Wi-Fi: A Forgotten Bottleneck for Collaborative Edge LLM Inference (Wang, Du, Xu, Liew; arXiv 2608.02341, 3-4 Aug 2026) [catalog says WDMoE; WDMoE itself not opened]
setting: Qwen3-30B-A3B (8 of 128 experts), 1 main + 8 worker + 1 predictor node, each one RTX 3090, 10 Gbps LAN; NS-3 Wi-Fi simulation at 1, 2 and 5 m
headline: UDP broadcast with retransmission gives 1.4x over NCCL/TCP on the wired 8-node cluster; 802.11 broadcast capped at 54 Mbps while optimal simulated rates are 64x/43x/32x higher at 1/2/5 m
transfers_to_us: no: activations are sent to expert hosts, weights stay put; GPU nodes
caveat: Paper is about broadcast of embeddings, not weight streaming; WDMoE is not the page opened (unverified).
notes: Wi-Fi 54 Mbps statement is accurate for this paper.

title: Multi-node local LLM inference guide 2026 (fungies.io, 1 Jul 2026)
setting: generic guide, llama.cpp RPC and vLLM
headline: page has no 200B MoE tok/s and no per-token sync figure; its tables contain arithmetic errors (e.g. 405B FP16 on ten 4090s) and unsourced throughput
caveat: Low-credibility, partly self-inconsistent page; catalog numbers (4-8 tok/s, 16 ms sync) are not on it.
notes: Replace by an actual benchmark source for RPC over 10GbE before citing.

title: Elbow-Based MoE Routing: A Training-Free Inference Time Plugin for Expert Selection (Pan, Liu, Fang, Andrei, Wu; Harvard; ICLR 2026 TTU Workshop; arXiv 2608.04401v1, 5 Aug 2026)
setting: OLMoE-1B-7B, cap K=8, six multiple-choice benchmarks; latency is wall-clock per forward pass (hardware not stated in the pages read)
headline: Table 2: mean k 7.62 of 8, FLOPs 5.37e8 to about 4.9e8, latency e.g. 11.203 to 10.497 ms (ARC-Easy), 5.3% average; accuracy within 0.33 points
transfers_to_us: no: removes only about 5% of experts (k 7.6 of 8), single small model, batch/hardware unspecified
caveat: Workshop paper, one model, forward-pass latency not decode; says nothing about k=4.
notes: Evidence for adaptive k is that tail experts are noise, but the gain is tiny.

title: HookMoE: A learnable performance compensation strategy of Mixture-of-Experts for LLM inference acceleration (Cheng, He, Li, Xie, Li; EMNLP 2025 main, pp 31594-31606)
setting: four MoE models (names not on the abstract page); hardware not on the page; PDF text not readable
headline: >50% fewer activated experts, 1.42x speedup that applies to the prefill stage only, about 2.5% average degradation (abstract)
transfers_to_us: no: prefill-only, needs a calibration/training step
caveat: No decode-stage number; setup and tables unverified (PDF unreadable). Catalog url is a preview host and gave 404; aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1610 works.

title: Mixture Compressor for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs Gains More (MC-MoE; Huang et al.; ICLR 2025, TPAMI 2026; arXiv 2410.06270)
setting: Mixtral 8x7B and 8x22B only; 1.5-2.5 bit weight-only quantization plus token-level dynamic expert pruning; 2.5-bit 8x7B needs about 16 GB static / 19 GB running GPU memory
headline: dynamic pruning gives >10% extra compression; speedup and accuracy only in an unreadable image
transfers_to_us: no: 8-expert GPU models; pruning is dynamic skipping, not top-10 to top-4
caveat: No numbers verified beyond the README; the 4-of-10 regime is not tested.

title: A faster (maybe better) Qwen 3.5 122B (azampatti, NVIDIA Developer Forums, 29 Aug 2026)
setting: DGX Spark / GB10 only; router changed from 8 to 4 of 256 experts; patched vLLM
headline: 70+ tok/s coding with patch vs about 47-50 without; custom benchmark 50.7% (top-4 Int4) vs 51% and 47% for two Int4 variants; tool-call score 89-91/100
transfers_to_us: no: GPU, self-reported, custom benchmark; shows quality can be kept for 8 to 4 after healing
caveat: Only the shared expert was retrained (catalog says further training, which is accurate but narrower); not peer reviewed; the 70 vs 50 tok/s mixes the patch with the k change.
notes: Closest published analogue to a top-4 halving on a roughly 120B model.

title: Our own first screen R16 (internal file, not a paper)
setting: local file Runs/R16 Screen of the top 22 brainstorm idea families.md
headline: top-k 10 to 6 or 4: ceiling 4.57 to about 5.4-6 tok/s, 1.3x at 8 GB, accuracy-gated; names NAEE, LExI, REAP and the expert_used_count override as prior art

title: Delta Decompression for MoE-based LLMs Compression (D2-MoE; Gu, Li, Li, Zhu, Lee, Sun, Xue, Guo; HKUST, Birmingham, AISpeech; ICML 2025; arXiv 2502.17298)
setting: Mixtral-8x7B, DeepSeekMoE-16B, Phi-3.5-MoE, Qwen2-57B-A14B; A100 GPUs; speed at batch 64
headline: Table 2 average accuracy: Mixtral 0.63 orig, 0.60/0.57/0.52 at 20/40/60%; DeepSeekMoE 0.54/0.49/0.41 vs 0.56; Table 4: 313.29 tok/s at 80% vs NAEE 278.53, memory 34.8/26.1/17.3 GB at 60/70/80%
transfers_to_us: no: GPU, batch 64, FP16-style baseline, compression ratio vs full-precision, and quality loss is already 10 points at 60%
caveat: Speed gain over other compressors is only 2-12%; 60% compression costs about 0.11 in average accuracy on Mixtral. Page notes a 6.46 vs 6.35 perplexity inconsistency.
notes: Compression is relative to 16-bit weights, so versus a 4.3-bit baseline the saving is much smaller (our break-even rank 150 at fp16 factors).

title: Sub-MoE: Efficient Mixture-of-Expert LLMs Compression via Subspace Expert Merging (Li, Zhu, Wang, Li, Gu, Han, Guo; arXiv 2506.23266v1, 29 Jun 2025)
headline: Table 1 retention: Mixtral about 96%/87% at 25%/50% reduction (abstract says 86%); Qwen3-30B-A3B about 87%/83%; Table 2 Mixtral tok/s 87.7 to 120.9 (6 experts, 30% intra compression) = 1.38x on 8 H800 (text says 1.1-1.3x)
transfers_to_us: no: merges experts (fewer experts), GPUs; retention at 50% is 77-87%
caveat: Percentages are the fetcher's own calculation from Table 1; quality cost is visible by 50%.
notes: Expert merging, not per-expert residual; closer to reducing expert count.

title: MoBE: Mixture-of-Basis-Experts for Compressing MoE-based LLMs (Chen, Ha, Lan, Zhang, Li; Inclusion AI; arXiv 2508.05257v1, 7 Aug 2025)
setting: Ling-Lite, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507, DeepSeek-V3-0324 (671B), Qwen3-235B, Kimi-K2 (1T); H100 GPUs
headline: Table 3: MoBE retains 96-99% accuracy at 15-30% compression (e.g. Qwen3-30B 78.6 to 75.8 at 24%; D2-MoE 66.4 at 24%); about 1.4% average drop; no latency reported
transfers_to_us: no: no speed numbers; shows that even good methods compress only 15-30% of parameters
caveat: Authors say it needs a custom mega-kernel (currently calls fused-MoE several times). Retention percentages are fetcher's calculation.
notes: Strongest evidence that the 50%+ SVD compression assumed by the screen costs quality.

title: Effective MoE-based LLM Compression by Exploiting Heterogeneous Inter-Group Experts Routing Frequency and Information Density (RFID-MoE; Mi et al.; arXiv 2602.09316v1, 10 Feb 2026)
setting: Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507 (main), DeepSeekMoE-16B, Qwen2-57B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen1.5-MoE, Ling-mini, Qwen3-235B; 8x A100
headline: Qwen3-30B at 60%: average zero-shot 0.64 vs 0.61 MoBE vs 0.66 original; PTB perplexity 16.92 vs 24.93 MoBE; no speed results
caveat: Catalog says never-activated experts get zero rank; the paper explicitly rejects that (rank floor of 1, low-utilised experts hold information).
notes: Rank allocation fuses effective rank and routing frequency (xi about 0.7-0.8).

title: REAL: low-rank compression of the weakest experts (GitHub anzr299/REAL; no paper named)
setting: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it; GSM8K and MMLU; hardware not stated
headline: 50% expert fraction: Qwen baseline GSM8K 87.87, SVD rank 256 89.08 but MMLU about 23 (baseline 83.73); Gemma SVD rank 88 GSM8K 84.08, MMLU 64.14 chat (baseline 83.83)
transfers_to_us: no: in-place reconstruction experiment; memory savings explicitly out of scope
caveat: Results are mixed and model-dependent; MMLU collapses to near chance on Qwen at 50%.
notes: Not a llama.cpp change, as the catalog says.
